description:
pkix-ct/src/verify.rs:64, 152-156

```rust
use pkix_path::SignatureVerifier;

pub struct SctVerifier<V: SignatureVerifier> {
    logs: CtLogList,
    verifier: V,
}
```

The public surface of `pkix-ct` includes a generic bound on a trait
defined in `pkix-path`. When `pkix-path` cuts a major version that
changes `SignatureVerifier`'s method signature, error type, or
associated types, every signature in `pkix-ct` that mentions
`SctVerifier<V: SignatureVerifier>` is implicitly broken too —
`pkix-ct`'s own SemVer compatibility is tied to `pkix-path`'s.

Workspace internal coupling is the maintainer's choice but it has
caller consequences: a downstream crate depending on `pkix-ct 0.x`
implicitly accepts the same major version constraint on `pkix-path`,
even if they never call `pkix-path` directly.

This pattern is fine within a tightly-coupled workspace where all
crates ship lockstep, but the Cargo.toml does not document the
expected coupling. Three improvements:

1. Add a `# Version coupling` section to the `SctVerifier` doc
   comment stating that `pkix-ct`'s SemVer follows `pkix-path`'s
   trait changes, and listing the pin: "pkix-ct 0.x.y requires
   pkix-path 0.x.y".

2. In Cargo.toml, use a tilde-version requirement on `pkix-path`:
   `pkix-path = { version = "~0.x", ... }`. (workspace inheritance
   currently obscures this; the workspace's [dependencies] section
   gets to set the version.)

3. (Optional) Re-export `pkix_path::SignatureVerifier` from
   `pkix-ct`'s public surface so callers can write
   `pkix_ct::SignatureVerifier` instead of pulling in `pkix-path`
   separately. This matches what's already done in `pkix-chain`'s
   role as umbrella crate.

Priority P2: the coupling exists either way; this is about making it
visible to callers so they can plan around it.
title: SctVerifier<V> re-export couples pkix-ct major version to pkix-path major version
